text:
Maria Gomez: FYI we need a new EKS cluster in us-west-2 for the APAC training queue migration. Need GPU nodepools (g5.4xlarge) + standard addons. Goal: prod-like, dedicated capacity, handoff to SRE by EOD Thursday.

Ken Liu: copying infra plan from notes. do we want spot for batch? :thinking: 

Maria Gomez: Prefer on-demand for initial bring-up. We'll consider spot autoscaling after validation.

Arjun Patel: I'll handle eksctl bootstrap. Using eksctl v0.120, here's the minimal nodegroup config I'll use:
```
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
metadata:
  name: rw-gpu-usw2
  region: us-west-2
nodeGroups:
  - name: gpu-g5
    instanceType: g5.4xlarge
    desiredCapacity: 4
    minSize: 2
    maxSize: 8
    iam:
      withAddonPolicies:
        imageBuilder: true
    labels:
      workload: inference
    taints:
      - key: gpu
        value: dedicated
        effect: NoSchedule
```

Tanya Baker: make sure the AMI is EKS-optimized with NVIDIA drivers (amazon-linux2 eks ami + cuda). We have a baked AMI ID in account `ami-0a1b2c3d` (devops image). Use that.

Ken Liu: CNI? we should use aws-vpc-cni with trunking enabled for higher pod density. Also set WARM_IP_TARGET and MINIMUM_IP_TARGET for gpu nodes.

Samir Rao: Don't forget nvidia-device-plugin daemonset and node-feature-discovery. I'll push manifests to infra repo. Also add the gpu-allocator plugin and metrics-exporter.

Maria Gomez: validation checklist before handoff:
- cluster created and control plane healthy
- nodes show gpu label and taint
- nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet Ready = n
- run nvidia-smi inside a GPU pod
- run simple inference workload (batched) and measure p50/p95 latency
- CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics flowing
- cost estimate validated against committed capacity

Arjun Patel: For validation I'll run:
kubectl get nodes -l workload=inference
kubectl describe node <node> | grep -i nvidia
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status ds/nvidia-device-plugin
kubectl run --rm -it nvidia-test --image=nvidia/cuda:11.7-base --restart=Never --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1' -- bash -c "nvidia-smi"

Tanya Baker: Common failure: "no devices found" -> usually driver mismatch or missing nvidia kernel module. Fix: use SSM to check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and compare kernel versions.

Ken Liu: Networking issue we hit before: ENI limits on c5n vs g5. Need to pick instance sizes with enough ENI / IPs OR enable trunking + secondary ENIs. Also update subnet route tables and make sure NAT gateways in private subnets.

Arjun Patel: For kube-proxy use IPVS mode for better pps. Also enable kubelet --protect-kernel-defaults=false? only if vendor AMI requires it.

Samir Rao: Instrument cost: per-hour on-demand g5.4xlarge ~ $2.40/hr (approx) — update in ticket. If we need dedicated reserved capacity for predictability, propose 3-year convertible reservations or Savings Plan.

infra-bot: Reminder: open PR to infra repo for nodegroup + addons. Template: /infra/clusters/us-west-2/gpu/README.md

Maria Gomez: Handoff docs to SRE:
- link to cluster in console
- eksctl config + terraform state
- AMI id and bake pipeline link
- runbook for driver failures + rollbacks
- Slack channel + paging policy
- cost ceiling and contact for capacity increases

Tanya Baker: Also add k8s Pod Security admission rules and namespace quotas to prevent noisy neighbors using all GPUs.

Ken Liu: After we validate, create a short smoke job that runs periodically using CronJob to surface regressions.

Arjun Patel: ETA: I'll create cluster tonight, run basic validation tomorrow morning, can hand off by 18:00 PST.

Maria Gomez: Thanks team. Ping me in thread when control plane is ready. I'll set up the perf tests.

Samir Rao: One more: for Dedicated we need to request ENIs increased for account in us-west-2 before scaling above 100 GPUs. File a support case if hitting limits.

Maria Gomez: noted. :thumbsup:
